metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Utah | Uinta & Paradox Basin Owners
metaDescription: A patient, portfolio-minded buyer for Utah mineral and royalty interests, including Uinta Basin waxy crude and SITLA-adjacent checkerboard acreage.
heroLead: For families holding Utah mineral and royalty interests, whether producing, quiet, or somewhere in between, and trying to decide what those interests are actually worth to their overall financial picture.
intro: We buy mineral and royalty interests across Utah, with particular depth in the Uinta Basin's waxy crude fairway and the Paradox Basin's gas trend in the southeast corner of the state. Most of the owners we talk with inherited their interest, often a fractional share split among several heirs from an original family allotment, and are trying to figure out what it's worth and whether selling makes sense for their situation right now.

We treat every conversation the way a family office would evaluate any other asset: look at the actual production history, understand the position relative to current drilling, and give you a grounded range you can compare against other options before you decide anything.

sections.heading: Why Utah mineral ownership is different
paragraphs: Utah's mineral map is a checkerboard. Sections of state trust land managed by SITLA sit interleaved with federal, tribal, and private minerals across much of the Uinta Basin, a legacy of the original statehood land grant. Split estate, where surface and mineral ownership were severed generations ago, is common as well. None of that makes an interest harder to sell, but it does mean title work here benefits from someone who has actually handled Utah deeds before, not a generic national buyer working from a template.

The Uinta Basin's oil is also genuinely distinctive. Its waxy black and yellow crude has to be heated to flow and is typically trucked or railed to Salt Lake refineries rather than moved by conventional pipeline, which shapes the price differentials and deduction lines you'll see on any royalty statement tied to this basin. We factor that reality into every valuation rather than treating your interest like it sits in a generic shale play.

sections.heading: How we approach a valuation
paragraphs: We start with your deed and recent royalty statements if you have them, look at production trend and decline behavior if the interest is producing, and weigh proximity to current drilling if it isn't. From there we can give you an honest range for your specific interest — we don't quote flat per-acre numbers sight unseen, because value here varies too much by county, play position, and title status to make that honest.
If leasing rather than selling looks like the better fit for your situation, we'll say so. We'd rather you make the right decision for your family than rush a sale that doesn't actually serve you.

sections.heading: What owners typically bring us
paragraphs: Producing royalty interests in Duchesne and Uintah counties tied to the Uinta oil fairway. Quiet, non-producing fractional interests inherited from an original homestead or allotment, sometimes split among several cousins who've never coordinated on what to do with the family's minerals. Paradox Basin gas interests in San Juan and Grand counties that have been leased for years without much recent activity. Whatever category yours falls into, the starting point is the same: send us your deed and any statements you have, and we'll walk you through what we see.

sections.heading: A patient process, not a rushed one
paragraphs: We don't attach expiration dates to the ranges we give, and we don't expect you to decide on our timeline. Some owners come to a decision within a week; others sit with the information for months before circling back, sometimes after settling an estate or coordinating with siblings who share the interest. Both are fine with us. Our role is to make sure you understand what you actually hold and what it's likely worth, whenever you're ready to act on that.

faqs.question: Do you buy mineral rights anywhere in Utah?
faqs.answer: We focus primarily on the Uinta Basin and Paradox Basin, where most of the state's active oil and gas mineral ownership sits, but we're happy to look at interests elsewhere in the state as well.

faqs.question: My family's interest has never produced anything. Is it worth anything?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, particularly if it's near current drilling activity, though the value reflects future probability rather than existing cash flow. Send us the deed and county and we'll give you an honest read.

faqs.question: How quickly can I get a range on what my interest is worth?
faqs.answer: Once we have your deed and, if available, recent royalty statements, we can typically give you a preliminary range within a few business days.

faqs.question: Is there any obligation to sell once I get an offer?
faqs.answer: None. Getting a range from us costs you nothing and commits you to nothing. Plenty of owners we talk with decide to lease or hold instead, and that's a fine outcome.

faqs.question: What if I'm not sure whether my minerals are in the Uinta Basin or the Paradox Basin?
faqs.answer: Tell us the county your acreage is in and we can generally tell you which play you're likely in, or point you toward how to confirm it from your deed's legal description.
